_: Copy this to .kbfix.json in your project, or to ~/.kbfix.json for the whole machine. Project wins over home. Every field is optional; what is shown here is the default.
_pair: The two languages to convert between, both ways. kbfix works on exactly TWO at a time: it is not a language detector, and it will not guess which of several languages you meant. Run --layouts to see what is installed (en, es, he, ru ship). Older forms still parse: "en-he" as a string, and the 0.2 "layouts" array, which is cut to its first two entries.
_minSignalChars: Below this many letters there is not enough evidence either way, so it says nothing. Lowering it will start guessing at things like /pr.
_minLetterDensity: Letters must be at least this fraction of the non-space characters. The models only read letters, so `if (a) { b(); }` would otherwise be judged on four of them, which happen to spell if/a/b and scored a perfect 1.0 as English.
_minTargetScore: How much the transposed text has to read like real prose, 0 to 1.
_minMargin: How far the transposition has to beat the text as typed. This is the gate that keeps ordinary prompts safe, because real prose scores near 1 in its own language and nothing can beat it by this much.
_minCandidateGap: How far the better reading has to beat the other one. Only applies to a same-script pair like en-es, where both directions are possible at once; a cross-script pair has exactly one candidate and this never bites.
